'''''Verbascum phlomoides''''', the '''orange mullein''', '''woolly mullein'''<ref name="RHS">{{cite web |title=Verbascum phlomoides |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/18802/verbascum-phlomoides/details |website=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=13 October 2021}}</ref> (which often refers to ''[[Verbascum thapsus]]''), or '''clasping-leaf mullein'''<ref name="histo">{{cite book |last1=Nowick |first1=Elaine |title=Historical Common Names of Great Plains Plants, with Scientific Names Index: Volume II: Scientific Names Index |date=2014 |publisher=Lulu.com |isbn=978-1609620608 |page=435 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=STTRCQAAQBAJ&dq=Verbascum+phlomoides+common+names&pg=PA435 |access-date=13 October 2021}}</ref>{{efn|The book reference by Elaine Nowick uses the word "mullen" instead of "mullein" twice in the common name. This is likely not a typo but an outdated use.}}, is a plant species in the family Scrophulariaceae native to Europe and Asia Minor. It is a widespread weed in North America. The [[Royal Horticultural Society]] considered it to be a good plant to attract pollinators.<ref name="RHS"/> It is used as a respiratory [[catarrh]] and [[diuretic]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=van Wyk |first1=Ben-Erik |last2=Wink |first2=Michael |date= 31 October 2018|title=Medicinal Plants of the World |page=366 |isbn=9781786393258  }}</ref>
